answer: A sybil farm is a yarrow: a thousand leaves above one hidden root. Weight each identity only by the count of DISTINCT honest reviewers who graded its work across a trailing window, drawn from one fixed orchard of graders. The clones share that root, so every alias draws from the same bounded orchard; histories overlap and each added leaf wins only a 1/N share, the credit delta per clone shrinking toward zero. Reviewer attention is a scarce outside input no coalition can mint or pool per clone; at settlement the ledger recounts each key's graders and burns credit behind any shared or kin edge.
